s1.syndrome_frame: chronic ulcerative skin lesion of the foot with a long history and lack of response to antifungal treatment
salient_findings: painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space
verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges
unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis on dermoscopy
key_facts: 60-year-old patient with no significant medical history
3-year history of macerated skin between the toes
18-month history of a progressively enlarging ulcer
lack of response to topical sertaconazole and oral terbinafine
ulcer measures 3 cm in diameter and extends onto the dorsum of the foot
ulcer has a whitish, fissured base and hyperkeratotic edges
dermoscopy reveals unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis
no palpable popliteal and inguinal lymph nodes

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: chronic ulcerative skin lesion with hyperkeratotic edges and lack of response to antifungal treatment

shortlist.label: Verrucous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: verrucous, infected ulceration with hyperkeratotic edges and whitish, fissured base

shortlist.label: Chronic venous leg ulcer
shortlist.why_kept: long history of macerated skin between the toes and ulcer extending onto the dorsum of the foot

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: progressively enlarging ulcer with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and lack of response to antifungal treatment

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: ulcer with a whitish, fissured base and hyperkeratotic edges, although less likely than squamous cell carcinoma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and a whitish, fissured base, along with dermoscopy revealing unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis, is consistent with verrucous carcinoma. The lack of response to antifungal treatments and the progressive enlargement of the ulcer also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the specific description of the ulcer as verrucous and the dermoscopy findings more strongly suggest verrucous carcinoma

rejected.label: Chronic venous leg ulcer
rejected.why: The location and description of the ulcer do not typically match those of chronic venous leg ulcers, which are usually found on the lower leg

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: The ulcer's appearance and the lack of systemic symptoms or other skin lesions make pyoderma gangrenosum less likely

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The description of the ulcer as verrucous and the location on the foot are not typical for basal cell carcinoma, which is more commonly found on sun-exposed areas
